samples.summary: Format painter (Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V) silently loses its ability to REMOVE B/I/U/S now that toggle-off clears the key instead of storing `false`
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:869 captures the painter buffer as the RAW caret run style (`this.styleBuffer = { ...this.getStyleAtCursor() }`, and `getStyleAtCursor` is documented at :2942-2949 as raw run style), and :1013 applies it via `applyStyleToSelection(range, this.styleBuffer)` → `Doc.applyInlineStyle` → `mergeInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:316-325), which only merges keys that are PRESENT in the patch. Before this PR a run that the user had un-bolded carried an explicit `bold: false`, so copying its formatting onto bold text un-bolded it. With `styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:399-418) the key is deleted from the run, so the painter buffer no longer contains `bold`/`italic`/`underline`/`strikethrough` at all and pasting the format onto bold/italic target text leaves the target's formatting in place. Neither call site was updated to compensate (e.g. by materialising explicit `false`/`undefined` for the boolean keyset when capturing). Fix belongs at the painter capture site, or by having the painter capture the full boolean keyset.

samples.summary: Clearing a boolean key now makes the local cached document merge adjacent runs while the Yorkie Tree keeps them split — local view and reloaded/collaborator view of the same block disagree on run segmentation
samples.evidence: YorkieDocStore.applyStyle updates its cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1770 for applyStyles and the equivalent call on the applyStyle path), which ends in `normalizeInlines` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:76-86) and merges neighbours whose styles are strictly equal. The Tree write path only removes EMPTY inlines ("Step 6: Clean up empty inlines produced by boundary splits", yorkie-doc-store.ts:1889-1893) and never merges two identical inline nodes, and the parse path (yorkie-doc-store.ts:418-426) does not normalise either. Before this PR a toggle-off stored `bold:false`, which is never equal to `undefined`, so the two representations stayed in step; now every B/I/U/S toggle-off can merge runs locally that remain split in the CRDT, so run counts (and anything derived from them, e.g. the hunt bridge's per-run reader at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:132-154) differ before and after a reload/remote sync.

verdict.reason: Every step of the claimed chain reproduces in the repo. The painter captures the RAW run style (text-editor.ts:869 -> getStyleAtCursor at :2949 -> caretInlineStyle with withStyleDefaults=false, caret-style.ts:46-66), and applies it as a partial patch (text-editor.ts:1013 -> applyStyleToSelection :2921-2940 -> Doc.applyInlineStyle document.ts:375-380). mergeInlineStyle (block-helpers.ts:316-325) only affects keys present in the patch, so an absent boolean key leaves the target untouched. styleOffAsClear (document.ts:399-418) now deletes a toggled-off boolean key from the stored run (except when the named style supplies it), and toggleStyle (text-editor.ts:2858-2903) is what feeds it the explicit `false`. Consequently a de-bolded run no longer carries `bold: false`, so Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V can no longer remove B/I/U/S from the target — a behaviour change to a shared write path whose out-of-diff consumer was not updated. No compensating materialisation exists (BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS is referenced only inside document.ts:405), and no guard makes the path unreachable: the shortcut is live in the keydown handler. Real and blocking under the blast-radius rubric (changed contract, unupdated consumer).

finding.summary: Toggle-off now emits a Yorkie `removeStyleByPath` op on the hottest editing path (B/I/U/S); if Yorkie history cannot reverse TreeStyleRemove, Cmd+Z after a toggle-off silently stops restoring the flag
finding.evidence: With the demotion in `Doc.styleOffAsClear`, every B/I/U/S off-toggle now reaches `YorkieDocStore.applyStyleInTree` with the key set to `undefined`, so `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163) returns the attr and `tree.removeStyleByPath(...)` runs at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1881 — previously only `styleByPath` ran for a toggle-off (the `false` was serialized), and `removeStyleByPath` was reached only by the rare removeLink / clear-formatting paths. Docs undo is Yorkie-history based (`this.doc.history.undo()` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2611), so the reversibility of the removeStyle op is now load-bearing for the most common formatting action in the product. I could not verify the SDK's reverse-op support from this checkout (the Yorkie SDK is not installed in node_modules here); confirming needs a collab/integration run that toggles bold off and then undoes it against a real Yorkie doc. Fix, if real, belongs in the Yorkie store (emit a compensating style write) rather than in the new Doc code.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is accurate (styleOffAsClear demotes false→undefined at document.ts:399-418, applied at document.ts:377 and :431; removedInlineStyleAttrs at yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163 then drives tree.removeStyleByPath at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1888; undo is Yorkie-history based at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2618). But the claimed consequence — that Cmd+Z after a toggle-off silently stops restoring the flag because the remove op may be irreversible — is refuted by a concrete counterexample in the repo: packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:214-228 performs applyStyle({bold:true}) → applyStyle({bold:undefined}) (which serializes to {} and therefore takes the removeStyleByPath branch) → undo asserts bold===true restored → redo asserts it cleared again. That test runs against the real SDK, not a mock: test:1-3 imports `yorkie from '@yorkie-js/sdk'` with no vi.mock, beforeEach (test:26-36) builds a genuine yorkie.Document/yorkie.Tree, `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.16 is a declared dependency (packages/frontend/package.json:93), and no vitest alias substitutes it. The test is not skipped, whereas the same file explicitly `.skip`s the Yorkie undo cases that genuinely are unsupported with TODO(yorkie-undo) markers (test:242-244, 296-300), so a live assertion here is an affirmative statement that the reverse op works. The reviewer's stated inability to verify came from an un-installed node_modules in their checkout, not from an absence in the repository. The behaviour is also documented as intended at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1877-1881 and docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:275-278, both citing that same test as the guard. If that test were in fact failing, the merge gate would catch it mechanically and independently of this finding.
